title: Structured Offboarding and Transition Playbook
author: Elena Park
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook defines a standardized, auditable offboarding and transition process for Redwood Inference employees and contractors. It balances security (timely deprovisioning), continuity (knowledge transfer and role handoff), and people-first exit practices (respectful communication, outplacement resources, and actionable feedback).

Scope:
- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and interns departing Redwood Inference for any reason (resignation, termination, role change, end of contract).
- Includes systems deprovisioning, IP and data controls, knowledge-transfer expectations, manager compliance steps, and reuse/rehire assessment.

Owner and escalation:
- Document owner: People Ops (owner: Elena Park).
- Operational steward: HR Operations (primary contact: hr-ops@redwood.ai).
- Escalation: Head of People Ops -> Legal (for compliance questions) -> Security (for suspected data exfiltration).

Key SLAs and success metrics:
- Account deprovisioning completed within 72 hours of termination; 4 hours for high-risk departures (SLA: 95%).
- Access suspension for voluntary resignation: within 24 hours of first notice if requested by manager for transitions requiring immediate restriction (SLA: 90%).
- Knowledge-transfer artifacts submitted 5 business days prior to last day (target: 80% compliance).
- Exit interview completion rate: >= 80% within 10 business days.
- Time-to-replace tracked per role; offboarding completeness < 5 business days post departure (success metric).

Checklist and timeline (manager + HR responsibilities)

T-30 to T-15 (when notice received or HR informed)
1. Confirm departure details and last working day with employee; log in HRIS.
2. Manager: start role transition plan and identify interim owner(s).
3. HR: schedule an offboarding intake meeting and calendar resignation/termination tasks.
4. Manager + employee: agree on knowledge-transfer deliverables and shadow schedule.

T-14 to T-5
- Employee: prepare Knowledge Transfer (KT) packet (see template below) and update runbooks, repos, and ticket queues.
- Manager: identify recipients of KT, schedule handover sessions.
- Security: review device and data access lists for high-risk access.

T-4 to T-1
- IT: prepare device return instructions and remote wipe schedules; ticket created in ITSM (ticket example: ITSM-12345).
- Finance: finalize expense reimbursements and last payroll items.
- People Ops: schedule exit interview and provide offboarding resource pack (benefits continuation, references, career transition services).

Day 0 (last day)
- Manager: conduct final handoff meeting and confirm KT completion.
- IT/Security: deprovision accounts per the deprovisioning matrix.
- HR: complete separation paperwork and record reason for departure.

Post-departure (T+1 to T+5)
- Verify all hardware received and any access revoked; close open tickets.
- Manager: reassign active work and update hiring intake if replacement required.
- People Ops: send follow-up exit-survey and compile findings.

Knowledge Transfer (KT) packet template (required items)
- Role summary: responsibilities, daily/weekly cadence, key stakeholders and contacts.
- Active projects: status, owners, current blockers, next 3 milestones and expected completion dates.
- Access map: list of repositories, dashboards, service accounts, and permissions needed (owner + help contact).
- Operational runbook snippets: start/stop procedures, incident playbooks, common commands, and known quirks.
- Recommended hires/skills for replacement: profile, must-have skills, and suggested interview prompts.

Example KT markdown snippet:

```
# KT: Payments Model Serving
Owners: @alice (prod), @bob (infra)
Status: In-flight. Next release: 2027-02-18
Important steps:
 - rebuild container: ./ci/build.sh --service=payments
 - rotate KV cache before migration: scripts/rotate_kv_cache.sh
Open tickets: RW-4557 (data drift investigation)
```

Security & access controls (deprovisioning matrix)
- Priority 1 (High risk): root/cloud-admin, KMS/HSM keys, production DB admin, access to customer PII. Deprovision within 4 hours of termination.
- Priority 2: Application owners, CI/CD tokens, production deploy keys. Deprovision within 24-72 hours.
- Priority 3: Read-only dashboards, non-sensitive repos. Deprovision per schedule but confirm within 5 business days.

Suggested commands and runbook snippets (IT ops)
- Revoke AWS console access (IAM): aws iam delete-login-profile --user-name <user>
- Disable GitHub access (org-level): gh api -X PATCH /orgs/redwood/memberships/<user> -f role=none
- Device wipe (example): ./tools/wipe-device.sh --serial S123456789

Legal and IP considerations
- Ensure signed Employment Agreements and IP Assignment are recorded in HRIS before final payout.
- For terminations with potential IP concerns, consult Legal before data export or copies are permitted.
- Preserve relevant communications if placed on legal hold; Security & Legal will instruct on scope and retention.

Exit interviews and continuous improvement loop
- People Ops conducts a structured exit interview within 10 business days of departure (phone or video).
- Exit data captured via a standard form: reason for leaving, manager effectiveness, onboarding experience, team dynamics, and suggestions for improvement.
- Quarterly People Ops digest: anonymized exit metrics, themes, and recommended changes to hiring/onboarding processes shared with People Ops leadership and Hiring Managers.
- Example action: if 30% of engineering exits cite unclear role expectations, update job descriptions and the new-hire onboarding checklist within 2 sprints.

Rehire / boomerang policy
- Eligibility window: former employees may be rehired after a minimum 90-day cooling period unless otherwise approved by Head of People Ops.
- Assessment criteria: performance at time of departure, reason for leaving, rehire eligibility flags (e.g., contractual restrictions).
- Rehire path: fast-track interview with manager and People Ops review; previous employment file appended to candidate profile.

Manager obligations and accountability
- Managers must complete the offboarding checklist in Workday (or HRIS) and confirm KT artifacts are available.
- Failure to complete checklist within SLAs will be reported monthly to People Ops and may affect manager performance review calibration.

Reporting and dashboards
- Offboarding dashboard (People Ops/Analytics): offboarding completion rate, mean time to deprovision, KT compliance rate, reason-for-leave heatmap, rehire rate.
- Monthly report cadence: People Ops -> People Leadership (1st Monday of month) with top 3 trends and recommended interventions.

Appendix: templates and forms
- Offboarding checklist (copy to manager): 1) Confirm last day in HRIS; 2) Create KT packet; 3) Schedule knowledge transfer sessions; 4) Request device return; 5) Submit access removal ticket; 6) Complete exit interview scheduling.
- Exit interview standard questions (short list): What prompted your decision? What went well? What didn\u2019t? Suggestions for improvement? Would you consider returning?
- Sample handover email (to stakeholders):

Subject: Handover: [Employee Name] - [Role] - Last day [Date]
Body: Hi team, as [Employee] prepares to leave on [Date], please find the KT packet here: [link]. Primary interim authors: [names]. Outstanding items: ...

Change history and governance
- Version 1.0 (2026-03-15): Initial published playbook.
- Version 1.2 (2026-11-02): Added deprovisioning matrix and SLA targets.
- Version 2.0 (2027-01-10): Introduced boomerang policy and manager accountability clause.
